A grid of rows and columns in a database that holds one kind of data.
A built-in part of PostgreSQL that lists the tables and columns that exist.

used_by: The db:schema command in the root package.json, which runs it through scripts/local/with-env.mjs.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and database address
sections.what: Brings in the tools it needs, finds the schema file, and reads the database address. It stops with a helpful message if the address is missing.
sections.why: Failing early with a clear instruction is kinder than a confusing error later.
sections.watch_out: The schema path is built from this file's location, so moving the file breaks the path.

sections.name: client
sections.title: Empty-database check and table creation
sections.what: Counts existing tables. If any exist, it refuses to run. Otherwise it runs the schema file, counts the tables again, and reports the total. It always closes the connection.
sections.why: Protects existing data from being overwritten.
sections.watch_out: The check looks only at two schema names. A database with data stored under other schema names would pass the check.

summary: Creates the full set of database tables on a brand-new, empty PostgreSQL database. It refuses to run on a database that already has tables.
purpose: First-time database setup for local development.
why: The header says it refuses to touch a database that already has tables, so existing data cannot be wiped by accident.
how: Reads the database address from the environment and stops with a message if it is missing. It connects and counts existing tables in the public and drizzle schemas. If there are none, it runs the schema SQL file from lib/db and counts the tables again to confirm. It closes the connection in every case.
inputs: The DATABASE_URL environment variable, and the lib/db/schema.sql file.
outputs: New database tables, a console message with the count, or a refusal message with a failing exit code.
risks: The check only looks at whether tables exist, not at what they contain. If the SQL file fails part way, the database may be left partly built, and the script does not clean that up.
debug: If it refuses to run, point DATABASE_URL at an empty database. If the schema file is not found, check the path and that lib/db/schema.sql exists. If it cannot connect, check DATABASE_URL and that PostgreSQL is running.
